sense: who lets a house or flat

evidence: Suet. Jul. 41.3: vīcātim per dominōs īnsulārum, street by street, through the landlords of the blocks of flats
Cic. Phil. 2.105: tē inquilīnō (nōn enim dominō), with you as tenant (for you were not the owner)
terms.comment: The owner, set against the tenant (inquilīnus); a landlady is domina.
The one who locat, lets (see rent, pay to use); a lawyers’ word.

phrases.latin: Recēnsum populī nec mōre nec locō solitō, sed vīcātim per dominōs īnsulārum ēgit
phrases.english: He took the count of the people neither in the usual way nor in the usual place, but street by street, through the landlords of the blocks of flats

sources: Lewis & Short: dominus · Lewis & Short: locator
